description: Controlled vocabulary defining canonical evidence types, provenance classes, reliability characteristics, and evidence-handling rules used by A.R.I.A. during microwave backhaul reasoning.

evidence_types.name: DIRECT_MEASUREMENT
evidence_types.description: A technical value obtained directly from equipment, an instrument, management system, or measurement device.

evidence_types.name: DIRECT_PHYSICAL_OBSERVATION
evidence_types.description: A physical condition directly observed by a person or captured clearly enough to establish the condition.

evidence_types.name: LIVE_EQUIPMENT_STATE
evidence_types.description: Current state reported directly by the applicable telecommunications equipment or management system.

evidence_types.name: EQUIPMENT_ALARM
evidence_types.description: Current or historical alarm generated by equipment or its management system.
evidence_types.notes: An alarm reliably establishes that the equipment reported the alarm condition but does not necessarily establish the alarm's root cause.

evidence_types.name: PERFORMANCE_COUNTER
evidence_types.description: Performance statistics or counters reported by equipment or a management system.

evidence_types.name: SYSTEM_LOG
evidence_types.description: Timestamped equipment, software, controller, or management-system log information.

evidence_types.name: LIVE_CONFIGURATION
evidence_types.description: Configuration retrieved directly from the equipment or authoritative management system.

evidence_types.name: CONFIGURATION_EXPORT
evidence_types.description: Exported configuration file or structured configuration dataset.

evidence_types.name: CONFIGURATION_SCREENSHOT
evidence_types.description: Screenshot showing equipment or management-system configuration.

evidence_types.name: EQUIPMENT_SCREENSHOT
evidence_types.description: Screenshot containing equipment state, measurement, alarm, configuration, or performance information.

evidence_types.name: FIELD_PHOTO
evidence_types.description: Photograph of equipment, installation, RF chain, antenna, path, cabling, connections, or another field condition.

evidence_types.name: VIDEO_EVIDENCE
evidence_types.description: Video recording containing relevant physical, equipment, installation, path, or operational evidence.

evidence_types.name: TECHNICIAN_STATEMENT
evidence_types.description: Technical observation, measurement, conclusion, or statement reported by a technician.

evidence_types.name: ENGINEER_STATEMENT
evidence_types.description: Technical observation, interpretation, design information, or conclusion reported by an engineer.

evidence_types.name: CUSTOMER_STATEMENT
evidence_types.description: Technical or operational information reported by a customer or customer representative.

evidence_types.name: USER_RECOLLECTION
evidence_types.description: Information supplied from memory rather than directly observed current evidence.

evidence_types.name: MANUFACTURER_DOCUMENTATION
evidence_types.description: Technical information published or formally supplied by the applicable equipment manufacturer.

evidence_types.name: MANUFACTURER_RELEASE_NOTE
evidence_types.description: Manufacturer-published release notes, defect information, compatibility information, or software-change documentation.

evidence_types.name: ENGINEERING_DESIGN
evidence_types.description: Approved path design, engineering package, RF design, configuration design, or equivalent engineering artifact.

evidence_types.name: CUSTOMER_STANDARD
evidence_types.description: Customer-issued technical requirement, standard, procedure, or specification.

evidence_types.name: INTERNAL_STANDARD
evidence_types.description: Validated internal Braxon or ARIA technical procedure, requirement, reference, or standard.

evidence_types.name: REGULATORY_STANDARD
evidence_types.description: Applicable regulatory, safety, licensing, or industry-standard technical information.

evidence_types.name: COMMISSIONING_RECORD
evidence_types.description: Recorded commissioning measurements, configuration, acceptance data, or closeout information.

evidence_types.name: AS_BUILT_RECORD
evidence_types.description: Documentation describing the installed physical or logical state of a completed system.

evidence_types.name: DIAGNOSTIC_TEST_RESULT
evidence_types.description: Result produced by a deliberate diagnostic test.

evidence_types.name: ISOLATION_TEST_RESULT
evidence_types.description: Result from a controlled test intended to determine whether a symptom follows a component, path, radio, configuration, or other variable.

evidence_types.name: BEFORE_AFTER_RESULT
evidence_types.description: Measured or observed difference before and after a controlled action.

evidence_types.name: CORRECTIVE_ACTION_RESULT
evidence_types.description: Observed technical outcome following a corrective action.

evidence_types.name: PRIOR_CASE
evidence_types.description: Relevant previously recorded troubleshooting or operational case.

evidence_types.name: AGGREGATED_CASE_HISTORY
evidence_types.description: Statistical or learned pattern derived from multiple historical cases.

evidence_types.name: USER_HISTORY
evidence_types.description: Validated historical pattern associated with a specific user's previous cases, actions, errors, observations, or outcomes.

evidence_types.name: PRODUCT_HISTORY
evidence_types.description: Validated historical pattern associated with a specific product, family, variant, revision, or configuration.

evidence_types.name: MANUFACTURER_HISTORY
evidence_types.description: Validated historical pattern associated with equipment from a specific manufacturer.

evidence_types.name: DETERMINISTIC_CALCULATION
evidence_types.description: Evidence derived through a defined deterministic mathematical operation from known inputs.

evidence_types.name: DERIVED_PATTERN
evidence_types.description: A structured pattern derived from multiple observations or evidence items.
examples: Both Diversity paths are approximately 16 dB below both Main paths

evidence_types.name: WEATHER_DATA
evidence_types.description: Observed, measured, or authoritative weather information relevant to the microwave path.

evidence_types.name: ARIA_INFERENCE
evidence_types.description: A conclusion or interpretation generated by ARIA from other evidence.
evidence_types.notes: ARIA inference is never self-validating evidence and must retain links to the evidence from which it was derived.

evidence_types.name: UNCLASSIFIED_EVIDENCE
evidence_types.description: Relevant information that cannot yet be mapped confidently to another canonical evidence type.

reliability_levels.VERY_HIGH: Evidence has strong direct diagnostic value and is produced through a controlled or highly discriminating observation or test.
reliability_levels.HIGH: Evidence is generally dependable when authenticity, applicability, and freshness are established.
reliability_levels.MODERATE: Evidence is useful but should normally be corroborated when materially affecting diagnosis.
reliability_levels.CONTEXT_DEPENDENT: Reliability cannot be assigned without considering source, user history, method, applicability, corroboration, and case context.
reliability_levels.DERIVED_ONLY: Information is derived from other evidence and shall not increase confidence merely because ARIA generated it.
reliability_levels.UNKNOWN: Reliability has not yet been established.

semantic_rules.rule: Evidence shall preserve provenance whenever provenance is known.
Evidence reliability and diagnostic relevance are separate properties. Highly reliable evidence may have little relevance to a particular hypothesis.

A human statement shall not automatically receive a fixed reliability weight solely because of the person's role. Historical accuracy, directness of observation, corroboration, technical context, and evidence type may affect its weight.
User-specific history may influence the weight assigned to future user-reported evidence but shall not cause ARIA to automatically reject contradictory direct evidence.
Direct current evidence shall generally outweigh historical expectation when the two materially conflict, provided the direct evidence is valid and applicable.
Historical case frequency may modify prior probability but does not prove the cause of the current case.
ARIA-generated inference shall retain traceable references to the evidence from which it was derived and shall never be treated as independent corroboration of itself.
Two evidence items derived from the same underlying source shall not be treated as independent corroboration merely because they are represented separately.

Evidence shall be evaluated for applicability to the exact manufacturer, product, product variant, hardware revision, firmware, topology, frequency band, configuration, scope, and other relevant context when those distinctions matter.
Evidence that has been superseded or invalidated shall remain historically traceable but shall not continue contributing active diagnostic weight.
Contradictory evidence shall be preserved and investigated rather than silently discarded.
The absence of expected evidence may itself become diagnostic evidence only when ARIA can establish that the evidence should reasonably have been present.
Before-and-after and isolation-test evidence may receive high diagnostic weight when the tested variable was sufficiently controlled and alternative explanations were reasonably constrained.
A document's authority does not guarantee applicability. ARIA shall distinguish whether authoritative documentation applies to the exact equipment and context under investigation.
Evidence confidence shall not be increased merely by repetition of the same claim across dependent or duplicated sources.
